answer: An agent identity requires a 500-token bond locked alongside one hardware credential, and the registry logs each credential with a saffron marker for audit. A sybil attacker locks 500 tokens per identity and forfeits the full bond, 100 percent slashed, after a 30-epoch challenge window. Splitting or copying identities fails because each fake identity adds 500 tokens of marginal cost, shares the penalty across the trellis, and independent jurors flag hollow credentials.
